display.purpose: Deck-card title over the photo scrim (32px/800); scales to 40px for the match eyecatch and 42px for the wallet balance figure.

title.purpose: Section headers, sheet headings, topbar and back titles (20-26px band, 700, tight tracking).

body.purpose: Base UI text at 16px; emphasized rows go 700 at 16-17.5px; secondary body is 14.5px muted.

label.purpose: Field labels, status lines, dock items, badges (13-14.5px, 600-700). The wordmark tagline is the only uppercase tracked-out text.

shadows.name: shadow-soft
shadows.purpose: Resting cards, list rows, deck actions, toasts.

shadows.name: shadow-card
shadows.purpose: Deck card, dock, credential passes, modals, match imagery - anything hovering over the world.

shadows.name: shadow-btn
shadows.purpose: Primary green buttons and the apply deck-action only; the shadow is tinted with the button's own green.

motion.name: ease-spring-out
motion.purpose: All entrances (rise-in, sheet-in, dock-in, pop-in) and the deck snap-back.

motion.name: rise-in
motion.purpose: Content entrance: fade + 14px rise (.anim-rise; dock uses 0.28s).

motion.name: pop-in
motion.purpose: Match image: scale 0.72 and -8deg settling to -4deg.

motion.name: press
motion.purpose: Buttons scale to 0.97 (deck actions 0.92); background swaps on press.

motion.name: deck-snap-back
motion.purpose: Card returns to rest after an uncommitted drag; drag itself is untransitioned pointer-driven transform (rotate 0.055deg/px).

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: prefers-reduced-motion: reduce collapses every animation and transition.

breakpoints.name: desktop-stage
breakpoints.purpose: The only media query: adds fixed lilac/apricot radial corner washes behind the centred 400px column. No responsive layout changes exist.

zScale.name: z-dock
zScale.purpose: Dock pill and open dock (scrim at 39).

zScale.name: legacy-modal-ladder
zScale.purpose: Preserved app flows: Modal/SubclaimModal/PdfPreview (100), collectionForm overlays (1200), background setup (1500), signing (2000), logging out (2100), PIN / Yoma-mismatch prompts (2200). Design-system overlays must stay below 100.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The one green action per decision context: full pill, green-glow shadow, presses down physically.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 8px; border: none; font-family: Nunito, system-ui, sans-serif; font-weight: 700; font-size: 16px; border-radius: 999px; padding: 15px 24px; background: var(--green-primary, #387f6a); color: #fff; box-shadow: 0 6px 18px rgba(56, 127, 106, 0.32); cursor: pointer; transition: transform 0.12s ease, background 0.15s ease, opacity 0.15s ease; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: var(--green-secondary, #2f6a59); } .ds-btn-primary:active { transform: scale(0.97); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--purple-primary, #54365d); outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-btn-primary:disabled { opacity: 0.45; cursor: default; }

components.name: Ghost Button
components.description: Deferring sibling of the primary: transparent pill with a 1.5px inset sand ring.
components.css: .ds-btn-ghost { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 8px; border: none; font-family: Nunito, system-ui, sans-serif; font-weight: 700; font-size: 16px; border-radius: 999px; padding: 15px 24px; background: transparent; color: var(--text-primary, #23202a); box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1.5px var(--border-color, #e5e2d4); cursor: pointer; transition: transform 0.12s ease, background 0.15s ease; } .ds-btn-ghost:hover { background: var(--surface-2, #efece0); } .ds-btn-ghost:active { transform: scale(0.97); } .ds-btn-ghost:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--purple-primary, #54365d); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Chip

components.name: Status Item
components.description: Tappable white list row: 52px thumb, bold title, muted meta, green status word.
components.css: .ds-status-item { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 12px; width: 100%; border: none; background: var(--surface, #ffffff); border-radius: 18px; padding: 12px 14px; box-shadow: 0 2px 10px rgba(50, 40, 60, 0.09); text-align: left; cursor: pointer; font-family: Nunito, system-ui, sans-serif; transition: background 0.15s ease; } .ds-status-item:hover, .ds-status-item:active { background: var(--surface-2, #efece0); } .ds-status-item__thumb { width: 52px; height: 52px; border-radius: 14px; flex: none; background: linear-gradient(135deg, #84a98c, #2f6b52); } .ds-status-item__body { flex: 1; min-width: 0; display: flex; flex-direction: column; } .ds-status-item__title { font-weight: 700; font-size: 16.5px; color: var(--text-primary, #23202a); } .ds-status-item__meta { color: var(--text-secondary, #5b5860); font-size: 14.5px; margin-top: 2px; } .ds-status-item__ok { color: var(--green-primary, #387f6a); font-weight: 700; font-size: 13.5px; flex: none; }

components.name: Text Field

narrative.overview: The opportunity is the interface. Home is a deck of full-bleed photo cards — one real, verified opportunity at a time — and everything else in the app is quiet support for that decision. The world is warm and paper-like: a beige ground, white 22px-radius cards floating on soft plum-tinted shadows, and Nunito set bold and tight everywhere. Chrome is summoned, never resident: navigation lives in a small floating pill until asked for, detail arrives in bottom sheets, and feedback is a dark whisper-pill at the top of the screen. Color is rationed by meaning, not by decoration: aubergine speaks for the brand and AI, forest green is the one color of action, orange carries money, and yellow appears only at earned moments. Motion is CSS-only — spring-eased entrances and hand-rolled pointer physics on the deck — because low-end Android is the performance bar. A deliberate engineering trait: the token file keeps jambo's legacy variable names alongside the prototype's new names, so pre-existing screens retint themselves through the cascade.
keyCharacteristics: Warm paper ground, white cards, plum-tinted soft shadows — no grey, no dark bands.
One typeface (Nunito), bold by default, negative tracking that tightens as size grows.
Meaning-locked palette: green acts, aubergine brands, orange pays, yellow celebrates.
Summoned chrome: dock pill, bottom sheets, top toast whisper.
Fixed 400px mobile column at every viewport; CSS-only motion; nothing fabricated.

rules.name: The Earned Yellow Rule
rules.body: Yellow appears only at earned moments — payment shown on a card, the match celebration, a saved opportunity. It is never a decorative accent.

rules.name: The One Green Rule
rules.body: Forest green means "this is the action" (or "this succeeded"). One green-filled element per decision context; everything else defers with sand, ghost, or tint treatments.

rules.name: The Aubergine Is Not A Button Rule
rules.body: Aubergine identifies the brand, AI, and progress; it fills chat bubbles, badges and focus rings, but never a primary call-to-action — that is green's job.

rules.name: The Bold Ladder Rule
rules.body: Weight and tracking move together: 800/−0.02em for display, 700/−0.01em for titles, 600 for labels, 400 for reading text. Never set a heading below 700, and never track headings out.

rules.name: The One Face Rule
rules.body: Nunito everywhere. The only exception is --font-mono for on-chain addresses.

rules.name: The Under-100 Rule
rules.body: New design-system overlays (docks, sheets, interstitials, toasts) take z values on the 10–70 scale. Never claim 100+ — that ladder belongs to the preserved modal flows, in that order.

rules.name: The Warm Shadow Rule
rules.body: Every shadow is plum-tinted rgba(50, 40, 60, …) or self-colored (the green button glow). No neutral-black shadows, no hard offsets.

rules.name: The Contained Glow Rule
rules.body: A tint band must fade to transparent inside its own bounds (mask black 40% → transparent); a glow still visible at its boundary produces a hard horizontal edge, which this world forbids.

rules.name: The No Corner Rule
rules.body: If it can be a pill or a circle, it is. Rectangular surfaces never go below 12px radius.

rules.name: The Scrim Ink Rule
rules.body: Card text over photos is always white — theme-independent.

dos: Do build new screens on the scaffold: .screen → .topbar → .screen__scroll (+ .pad), with .bottom-cta for pinned actions and .dock-clear on anything that scrolls under the dock pill.
Do use the global grammar (.btn, .chip, .card, .status-item, .field, .sheet) before writing new CSS — the system already has a shape for most needs.

Do keep both token vocabularies alive: prefer the new names (--surface-2, --r-card, --shadow-soft) in new code, and leave the legacy aliases (--card-bg-color, --accent-color, --button-border-radius…) defined so untouched screens keep retinting through the cascade.
Do give every gesture a visible tap equivalent (deck action buttons mirror the swipes) and keep touch targets ≥ 42px.
Do color SVG strokes with currentColor or style={{ stroke: 'var(…)' }} — never a var() in a presentation attribute.
Do keep motion CSS-driven on the spring-out curve, and let prefers-reduced-motion kill all of it.
donts: Don't fabricate data to fill the comp's slots: payment/hours meta-pills, wallet activity, notifications feed, AI chat, and the Visa card are deliberately absent until real backing exists (see .impeccable/surfaces/screens-deck-tsx.md and screens-wallet-tsx.md). A surface shows real data or doesn't ship.
Don't add @media responsive layouts — the app is a fixed 400px column everywhere; the only breakpoint is the ≥501px desktop stage wash. No phone bezel on desktop.
Don't take z-index 100 or above for design-system overlays; the 100→2200 ladder belongs to the preserved modal flows.
Don't spend the reserved colors: yellow outside earned moments, aubergine as a call-to-action, orange for anything but money/attention, info-blue on new surfaces.
Don't add fonts, filled/glyph icon sets, animation libraries, pure-black shadows, or dark background bands (bands are light tints now — GradientBand).
Don't put technical jargon in user-facing copy — "Vault", never "Matrix"; money words, never token words.
